messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: hosted-api p95/p99 token latency spike detected in us-west-2 for generation endpoints. Queue depth for gpu-pool-hosted has grown from ~30 to 1200 in 6m. Auto-scale attempted. Escalating to on-call.

maya (oncall): I'm on it. seeing 503s start around 14:03 UTC, p99 > 12s, error rate up for tenant-heavy routes. tagging infra.

jonathan (infra): oncall_maya thanks. looking at autoscaler logs now. initial observation: autoscaler triggered scale-up but provisioning kept failing with provider quota errors.

arjun (sre): adding context: we've had a burst from a third-party partner pushing batch traffic — looks like many long-context requests. KV cache warmups are spiking memory.

maya (oncall): can we confirm whether this is pure capacity limit or an autoscaler bug? need ETA for mitigation and customer impact summary.

jonathan (infra): autoscaler tried 3x launches across hosts in us-west-2; cloud API returned 403 quota_exceeded for vGPU-type-A on each attempt. error snippet:
```
2026-03-14T14:05:12Z autoscaler-controller: createInstance failed: provider error: QuotaExceeded: requested 8, allowed 0 for vGPU-A
```

infra-bot: (annotation) deployed-revision: hosted-api/v2.7.3, autoscaler-config: scale_limit=200, scale_step=20, provider_region=us-west-2

arjun (sre): consequence: requests are queuing on API gateway because backend concurrency is saturated. We should short-circuit non-critical traffic and enable fallbacks.

anna (ops_lead): proposing immediate mitigations: 1) enable tenant-level throttles for heavy tenants, 2) enable model fallback to cpu-optimized small models for eligible routes, 3) emergency per-route reject policy for non-SLA plans. any objections?

maya (oncall): proceeding with (1) and (2) now. I'll post commands.

maya (oncall): throttling heavy tenants (tenant IDs redacted):
```
# apply temporary rate limit in gateway
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/limits -d '{"tenant":"T-xxxx","max_rps":10,"mode":"enforce"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP'
```

jonathan (infra): manual fallback routing enabled: model-routing rule updated to send non-critical traffic to rtd-small-quantized in us-west-2 and to fallback-hosted-cpu farm in us-east-1.

leah (cust-succ): heads up to CS — customer-facing SLOs may be impacted for Advanced plan customers on generation routes. prepping message templates.

maya (oncall): starting connected mitigation: evicting queued low-priority batch jobs from gpu-pool-hosted to free slots for interactive requests. Running:
```
kubectl -n inference exec -it autoscaler-ctrl -- /bin/sh -c 'python /opt/ctrl/evict_low_prio.py --pool gpu-pool-hosted --age 300'
```

arjun (sre): note: eviction helps but memory KV caches still heavy. suggestion: temporary max_seq_length reduction for new requests to cut memory pressure. pushing config change shortly.

jonathan (infra): update: provider quota team acknowledged emergency request; they can provision +40 vGPUs in ~18-25m but not instant.

maya (oncall): rolling out max_seq_length=2048 override for non-SLA traffic:
```
PATCH /config/serving_overrides
{"route_selector":"*.open.gen","overrides":{"max_seq_length":2048}}
```

infra-bot: reaction :white_check_mark: override applied to 8 routes.

arjun (sre): early signal: queue depth stopped rising after throttles + fallback; p95 dropped from 7.3s to 2.1s on unaffected routes, p99 still elevated (~9s) for long-context SLA traffic.

anna (ops_lead): customer impact: list of tenants with increased error-rate available in incident ops dashboard. Leah pls coordinate comms for affected enterprise customers.

leah (cust-succ): will notify top 8 impacted accounts with status + mitigation + ETA. ETA for capacity from provider ~25m per jonathan. Draft message ready.

jonathan (infra): follow-up: autoscaler controller logs show repeated reconcile failures due to node label mismatch on pool selector. We patched a failing validation rule in infra earlier this week; looks like it's skipping some instance types which triggers indirect quota requests to unavailable families. We'll open a post-incident fix.

maya (oncall): handoff: I'm still primary but going to hand to jonathan for next phase since this is infra-provisioning-heavy. jonathan, confirm you accept oncall?

jonathan (infra): I accept. I'll keep maya looped. moving to incident role: infra primary.

arjun (sre): monitoring: added temporary alert to detect queue > 400 and p99 > 8s; will remove once stable. Also capturing sample traces for regression debugging.

maya (oncall): summary for timeline (to record): detection 14:03 UTC; autoscaler attempted scale-up 14:04–14:06 (quota failures); throttles + fallbacks started 14:08; provider acknowledged emergency quota 14:12; manual evictions + overrides 14:09–14:15.

anna (ops_lead): next steps: (A) confirm provider vGPU increase and verify nodes join pool; (B) postmortem to include autoscaler validation bug and improved rate-limiting defaults; (C) customer comms by CS. assigning owners after handoff.

leah (cust-succ): posting customer note now:
"We’re currently mitigating an inference capacity issue impacting generation latency for some customers in us-west-2. We’ve enabled temporary rate limits and model fallbacks and are working with our cloud provider to add capacity. Estimated mitigation in ~30 minutes. We'll update in 20 minutes or as milestones hit."

jonathan (infra): provider just confirmed +32 vGPU capacity added at 14:28 UTC; nodes booting and joining cluster. kube join logs:
```
kubelet: node \"gpu-32-az1\" registered, labels: pool=gpu-pool-hosted, instanceType=vGPU-A
```

arjun (sre): p99 now trending down. queue drain in progress. keeping alerts for 1h after stabilization.

maya (oncall): closing loop: lowering page severity to MONITOR at 14:31 UTC. we'll start postmortem tonight. thanks team for quick ops. :raised_hands:
